text:
The purity of the Noble Eightfold Path <note>Sanskrit: aryastangamarga</note>, the purity of form <note>Sanskrit: rupa</note>, and the purity of the knowledge of all aspects <note>Sanskrit: sarvakarajñata</note> are non-dual. They cannot be divided into two, are not distinct, and are not separate. Through the purity of the Noble Eightfold Path comes the purity of sensation <note>Sanskrit: vedana</note>. Through the purity of sensation comes the purity of the knowledge of all aspects. In this way, the purity of the Noble Eightfold Path and the purity of sensation are <note>the text continues to establish the non-dual relationship between these factors of enlightenment and the aggregates</note>

<summary>This page discusses the ontological unity and purity of the Noble Eightfold Path, physical form, and the omniscience of a Buddha. It emphasizes the non-dual nature of these qualities within the framework of Prajnaparamita philosophy.</summary>
<keywords>Noble Eightfold Path, non-duality, purity, sensation, omniscience, Buddhist philosophy, Prajnaparamita</keywords>
